recipes.name: Poulet aux Noix (Chicken with Cashews)
steps: Prep: Cut chicken into serving pieces. Juice 1–2 limes. Mince 4–5 garlic cloves. Dice 1 onion, 1 bell pepper, and 2 tomatoes. Roughly chop 3/4 cup cashews.
Marinate: In a bowl, toss chicken with lime juice, half the garlic, 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp salt, and black pepper. Rest 20–30 minutes at room temperature.
Brown: Heat 2–3 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high. Brown chicken on all sides in batches; set aside.

Build sauce: In the same pot, saute onion and bell pepper until soft, 5 minutes. Add remaining garlic and cook 30 seconds. Stir in tomatoes and a pinch of salt; cook until they break down, 5–7 minutes.
Simmer: Return chicken and any juices. Add 1/2 cup water or stock and the cashews. Cover and simmer on medium-low 25–30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce is thick.
Finish: Taste and adjust salt, lime, and pepper. Serve with diri (rice) or bannann peze.

recipes.name: Diri Kole (Rice and Beans)
steps: Prep beans: If using dried beans, soak overnight or quick-soak. Drain. Cover with fresh water, add a sprig of thyme, and simmer until tender, 45–60 minutes. Drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid. (Canned beans: rinse and drain.)
Aromatics: Dice 1 onion and mince 3 garlic cloves. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot. Saute onion until translucent, then garlic for 30 seconds.
Toast rice: Add 2 cups rinsed long-grain rice. Stir 1–2 minutes until grains look slightly opaque.
Cook: Add beans, 1 cup coconut milk, reserved bean liquid (or water) to cover by about 1/2 inch, 1 tsp salt, and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Steam: Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook 18–20 minutes without lifting the lid. Rest off heat 5 minutes.
Finish: Fluff with a fork. Adjust salt. Serve as a side or main with pikliz.

recipes.name: Griot (Fried Pork)
steps: Prep: Cut 2–3 lbs pork shoulder into 1.5–2 inch chunks. Juice 2 limes and 1 orange. Mince 6 garlic cloves. Slice 1 onion. Leave Scotch bonnet whole or slit once for heat control.
Marinate: Combine pork with citrus juice, garlic, onion, 2 tsp thyme, 2 tsp salt, and the pepper. Mix well. Marinate at least 1 hour, preferably overnight in the fridge.
Boil: Transfer pork and marinade to a pot. Add water to barely cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer 45–60 minutes until pork is tender but not falling apart. Drain well.
Dry: Pat pork dry with paper towels — moisture prevents crispiness.
Fry: Heat 1–2 inches oil to 350F (175C). Fry pork in batches until deep golden and crisp, 4–6 minutes. Drain on a rack or paper towels.
Serve: Hot with pikliz, bannann peze, and rice. Squeeze extra lime over the top.

recipes.name: Soup Joumou (Pumpkin Soup)
steps: Prep: Cut 1–2 lbs stewing beef into chunks. Peel and cube 2 lbs pumpkin (or use kabocha). Dice onion, carrot, and celery. Mince garlic. Chop parsley.
Meat base: In a large pot, cover beef with water. Add onion, garlic, thyme, and salt. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer 45–60 minutes until beef is tender.
Vegetables: Add pumpkin, carrot, and celery. Simmer until pumpkin is very soft, 20–25 minutes.
Texture: Remove some pumpkin pieces and mash or blend them, then return to the pot for body.
Pasta: Add small pasta (or broken spaghetti) and cook until tender, 8–10 minutes. Add water if the soup is too thick.
Finish: Stir in parsley and a squeeze of lime. Taste for salt. Serve hot — traditionally on New Year's Day in Haiti.

recipes.name: Legim (Vegetable Stew)
steps: Prep: Cube 1 large eggplant. Shred 1/2 cabbage. Slice 2 carrots. Dice 1 onion and 2 tomatoes. Mince 3 garlic cloves.
Saute base: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wide pot. Cook onion until soft, then garlic 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and thyme; cook until saucy, 5 minutes.
Layer vegetables: Add eggplant and a pinch of salt. Cook 5 minutes, stirring. Add carrot, then cabbage. Mix gently.
Simmer: Add 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook on medium-low 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are soft and the stew is cohesive.
Finish: Taste and adjust salt. Some cooks mash part of the mixture for a thicker texture. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Bannann Peze (Fried Plantains)
steps: Prep: Use green (unripe) plantains. Cut off ends, score the peel lengthwise, and remove the skin. Cut into 1-inch thick diagonal slices.
First fry: Heat 1/2 inch oil to about 325F (160C). Fry plantain slices 2–3 minutes per side until pale gold and slightly soft. Do not brown deeply yet. Drain.
Smash: Place each piece between parchment or in a tostonera and press firmly into a flat disc about 1/4 inch thick.
Second fry: Raise oil to 350–360F (175–180C). Fry smashed plantains again until deep golden and crisp, 1–2 minutes per side.
Season: Drain on a rack. Sprinkle with salt while hot. Serve immediately with griot or as a side.

recipes.name: Tassot (Fried Beef)
steps: Prep: Cut 2 lbs beef (chuck or similar) into strips or chunks. Juice 2 limes. Mince 5 garlic cloves. Slice 1 onion.
Marinate: Toss beef with lime, garlic, onion, thyme, 2 tsp salt, and pepper. Marinate 1 hour or overnight.
Boil: Put beef and marinade in a pot with water to cover. Simmer 1–1.5 hours until tender. Drain thoroughly and pat dry.
Fry: Heat oil to 350F. Fry beef in batches until browned and crisp at the edges, 3–5 minutes. Drain.
Serve: With pikliz, plantains, and rice.

recipes.name: Pikliz (Spicy Pickled Slaw)
steps: Prep: Finely shred 1/2 small cabbage. Grate or julienne 2 carrots. Thinly slice 1 small onion. Slice 1–2 Scotch bonnets (remove seeds for less heat; wear gloves).
Combine: In a glass jar or bowl, mix cabbage, carrot, onion, and pepper. Add 1 tsp salt and black pepper.
Pickle: Pour white vinegar (or a mix of vinegar and lime juice) over the vegetables until fully submerged. Press down so everything is under liquid.
Rest: Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Flavor improves over 1–2 days.
Serve: As a sharp, spicy condiment with griot, tassot, fried fish, or rice. Keeps refrigerated 1–2 weeks.

recipes.name: Mayi Moulen (Cornmeal Mush)
steps: Liquid: In a pot, combine 2 cups water and 1 cup coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add 1/2 tsp salt.
Cornmeal: Whisk in 1 cup fine cornmeal in a slow stream to avoid lumps. Switch to a wooden spoon.
Cook: Stir frequently over medium-low heat 15–20 minutes until thick, smooth, and the raw corn taste is gone. Add water if it gets too stiff.
Finish: Stir in 1 tbsp butter or oil. Taste for salt. Serve soft as a side, or pour into a dish, cool, slice, and pan-fry.

recipes.name: Akasan (Corn Drink)
steps: Base: Whisk 1/2 cup fine cornmeal into 2 cups cold water until smooth.
Cook: Pour into a pot. Add 1 cinnamon stick and 1 star anise. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, 8–10 minutes.
Enrich: Gradually whisk in 2 cups milk. Simmer 5 more minutes. Remove spices.
Sweeten: Stir in sugar to taste (start with 3–4 tbsp) and 1 tsp vanilla.
Serve: Hot in mugs, or chill and serve cold. Stir before drinking if it thickens further.
